function: p. 6-9: Diffusion-enhanced SAC agent jointly controls UAV 3D trajectory, task offloading and GT uplink power for RSMA sub-messages to maximize energy efficiency; decoding order is analytic (Proposition 1).
system: p. 3-4, 9: UAV-mounted MEC server and K=2-5 ground terminals, uplink RSMA with two sub-messages and SIC, 2.4 GHz, 1 MHz; antenna count not stated; no RIS.
method: p. 6-9: Soft Actor-Critic with a DDPM diffusion-model actor (denoiser network) and double critics, online reinforcement learning on a replay buffer; learning rate 5e-4, 500 episodes.
data_channel: p. 3-4, 9: Simulated 1000x1000 m area, air-to-ground LoS-probability path-loss model [34] with parameters from [34], [44], 100 one-second slots; no dataset, the agent learns from environment interaction.
test_conditions: p. 9-12: Same simulated environment for training and evaluation; parameters swept (GT count 2-5, power, task size, time slots, UAV rate, bandwidth); no unseen-scenario test stated.
baselines: p. 9-10: PPO (PPORS) and DQN (DQNRS) agents, GDRS with random decoding order, and the same diffusion DRL under FDMA (GDFD) and NOMA (GDNO); no non-learned method.
metrics: p. 4, 10-12: Energy efficiency in bits/Joule, average reward over training episodes, and UAV 3D trajectories.
q1_support: p. 3: "Based on the air-to-ground propagation model for urban scenarios [34]"; Table I (p. 9) takes its constants from [34] and [44]. Custom simulator; no 3GPP TR 38.811 or 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 10: "under different numbers of GTs K" (Fig. 5); Figs. 5-9 (pp. 10-12) sweep parameters, but the paper never states that a trained policy is tested in another scenario or adapted to it.
q3_support: p. 9: "we compare our proposed GDRS method with the following" PPORS (PPO), DQNRS (DQN) and GDRS-Random ("UAV adopts the random decoding order for uplink GTs instead of optimal policy proposed in Proposition 1"); GDFD and GDNO (p. 10) reuse the diffusion DRL. Learned baselines exist, but no non-learned method (SCA, heuristic, fixed trajectory) is compared.
q4_support: p. 3: "we derive a lightweight priority-based RSMA strategy" is only qualitative. No complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime of GDRS is reported; Figs. 3-4 (p. 10) show reward versus training episode only.
q5_support: p. 9: "More parameters about the considered scenario and proposed method are shown in Table I". Custom simulation; no code or data link and no public dataset appear in the 13 pages.
notes: Borderline on Step 1 above_phy, for the reviewer to confirm. The action a(n) (p. 6) covers UAV movement and task offloading (above the physical layer) and the GT transmit powers of the two RSMA sub-messages (physical layer, aerial link): "task offloading and power control decisions". By the rule on joint decisions it passes, and area 6 was assigned (power control of an aerial link). The SIC decoding order is analytic (Proposition 1, pp. 5-6), not learned. If the reviewer reads the learning as trajectory and offloading only, the exclusion code would be above_phy. q1 is 0 because the Al-Hourani air-to-ground LoS-probability model [34] is neither a 3GPP or ITU model nor a public dataset. The PDF is the arXiv preprint (arXiv:2507.12910v1).
